children: The Bank of Canada's somewhat surprising hawkish turn this week might now look "somewhat premature" due to details in August's labor data, says Thomas Ryan of Capital Economics. Employment fell 41,700 in August although the unemployment rate remained unchanged at 6.4%. More notably, wage growth slowed sharply, to 2% from a year ago — or weakest 12-month increase in pay since 2021, or during the Covid-19 pandemic. "It is hard to question our and the BOC's assessment that the economy remains in excess supply," Ryan says of the wage-growth slowdown. August's labor data should temper talk of an immediate rate hike, he adds. (paul.vieira@wsj.com; @paulvieira)
